rv.q: This minimalism might be efficient, but it doesn't always serve the play, and makes it harder to create the claustrophobic, cigarette smoke-saturated feel of a tiny office that's full of caged corporate beasts.
In the main however, I found too many jarring incongruities to make it plausible.

cn.t: Mamet's durable classic gets an all-female cast in Marber's staging, but critics find it a missed opportunity. Strong individual performances can't overcome a production that lacks tension and fails to justify its gender-swap concept.
